tests.name: math
tests.description: The Math functions (abs, ceiling, exp, floor, ln, log, power, round, sqrt, truncate), the Math operators (*, /, +, -, div, mod) on Integer, Decimal and Quantity, unary + and -, Integer/Decimal promotion, division by zero, Integer overflow, the Decimal range and precision, quantity arithmetic with units (same unit, UCUM conversion to the most granular unit, products and quotients of units, numbers implicitly converted to quantities, calendar durations), what 3.0.0 adds (Quantity input to ceiling, floor, truncate and round, round of a negative half, errors in log, the left operand's unit when both are equally granular, special units, Long arithmetic and Long inputs through toLong) and FHIR values reaching these operators (including time-valued UCUM codes mapped to calendar units). Arithmetic on quantities of different units cites the sentences that make UCUM conversion conditional (2.0.0 SHOULD, 3.0.0 SHALL for an implementation that converts) and those that let an implementation without it return empty (MAY). + and & on strings are covered by strings.xml and not repeated. Leaves out what the text does not settle: the Integer result of an Integer raised to a negative Integer under 2.0.0, ties other than 0.5 and -0.5 for negative numbers in round, the precision (number of digits) of a Decimal result, Decimal overflow and underflow beyond the minimum range, ln of zero or a negative number, log with base 1, exp overflow, abs of the lowest Integer, div and mod by a Decimal zero, invalid units, special units with the same unit or with a number, units that are not commensurable (empty or error), the unit chosen when both quantities are equally granular in 2.0.0, division and multiplication of calendar durations by a number, 1 year + 12 'mo', the unit of 1 minute - 30 's', associativity of operators at the same precedence, and Long literals (5L), which the pinned grammar does not parse.

group.name: REQ-MATH-059
group.description: + and - of quantities in different units of the same dimension give the result in the most granular unit; conversion is a SHOULD in 2.0.0 and a SHALL in 3.0.0 for an implementation that converts UCUM, and an implementation without UCUM conversion may return empty instead
group.source: Implementations should support other unit functionality as specified by UCUM, including unit conversion.
Implementations that do not support complete UCUM functionality may return empty (`{ }`) for calculations involving quantities with units where the units are different.

Implementations that DO support UCUM conversions SHALL support implicit conversions where operations between quantities with different units are performed, and also explicitly through [toQuantity(unit)](#fn-toquantity).
Implementations that do NOT support UCUM unit conversion may return empty (`{ }`) for calculations involving quantities with different units.
Implementations that to not support processing UCUM units shall return empty when unable to correctly handle the units.

When operating on quantities, the dimensions of each quantity must be the same, but not necessarily the unit. For example, units of 'cm' and 'm' can be compared, but units of 'cm2' and 'cm' cannot. The unit of the result will be the most granular unit of either input.
When the units of quantity arguments are different, the quantity values must be [**converted**](#unit-conversions) to the most granular unit, then simple addition on the values can be performed.
3 'cm' + 3 'm' // 303 'cm' ; via ucum conversion to most granular unit
(3 'm' + 3 'cm').toQuantity('m') // 3.03 'm' ; as above except explicitly convert the result to meters
3 'cm' - 3 'm' // -297 'cm' ; ucum conversion to centimeters (most granular unit)
